record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Let X be an F-space equipped with an F-norm ||x||. Must there always exist an equivalent F-norm on X such that for every nonzero x, the function t ↦ ||tx|| for positive t is analytic?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1. - Let X be an F-space with a norm || x|| . Does always an equivalent analytic norm exist ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-norm on a real or complex vector space $X$ is a function $\|\cdot\|:X\to[0,\infty)$ such that: (i) $\|x\|=0$ iff $x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|\le\|x\|$ for every scalar $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le 1$; (iii) $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$; and (iv) $\|\alpha_n x\|\to 0$ whenever scalars $\alpha_n\to 0$, and $\|\alpha x_n\|\to 0$ whenever $\|x_n\|\to 0$. An F-space is a vector space equipped with an F-norm whose induced translation-invariant metric $d(x,y)=\|x-y\|$ is complete. Two F-norms on $X$ are called equivalent if they induce the same topology.

Question: Given an F-space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$, does there always exist an equivalent F-norm $\vertiii{\cdot}$ on $X$ such that for every nonzero $x\in X$, the function $t\mapsto \vertiii{tx}$ is real-analytic on the open ray $(0,\infty)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this problem on the existence of equivalent analytic F-norms on a general F-space. It is a long-standing question in the theory of metric linear spaces; no source located confirms a solution, but absence of evidence is not conclusive.
